title: Dede Westbrook's 232 Yards vs. Texas: Once OU's Receiving Record
question: Who holds Oklahoma's single-game receiving yards record?
answer: Marquise Brown holds it with 265 yards at Oklahoma State in 2017. Dede Westbrook set the mark first, with 232 yards and three touchdowns in a 45-40 win over Texas on Oct. 8, 2016.
summary: Dede Westbrook's 232-yard game against Texas in 2016 set an Oklahoma receiving record, since passed by Marquise Brown's 265 yards at Oklahoma State in 2017.
body: Dede Westbrook's 232-yard day against Texas was Oklahoma's single-game receiving record when he set it, though it has since been passed. On Oct. 8, 2016, the Sooners beat Texas 45-40 in Dallas, and Westbrook finished with 10 catches for 232 yards and three touchdowns.

His three scores covered 71, 42 and 47 yards, so almost all of his production came on explosive plays rather than short gains. Baker Mayfield threw for 390 yards in the game, and Westbrook was his favorite target all afternoon. Reports from Bleacher Report and Fox Sports described the 232 yards as an Oklahoma single-game receiving record at the time.

The offense around him was just as busy. Oklahoma piled up 672 total yards, and Samaje Perine ran 35 times for 214 yards and two touchdowns. The teams combined for 85 points, which kept the Sooners from ever relaxing against a Texas team that kept answering.

The game fit into a remarkable season for Westbrook. He went on to win the Biletnikoff Award as the nation's top receiver and finished the year with 1,524 receiving yards and 17 touchdown catches. Marquise Brown later took the single-game record with 265 yards at Oklahoma State in 2017, and Westbrook's 232 still ranks among the best receiving games in OU history.
